source.title: Physics Steering: Causal Control of Cross-Domain Concepts in a Physics Foundation Model
source.authors: R. Fear; Payel Mukhopadhyay; Michael McCabe; Alberto Bietti; Miles Cranmer

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether single activation directions can control physical concepts in Walrus, a physics foundation model, extending direction-based feature evidence to a new model setting. It does not test toy-model superposition or capacity competition.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative outcomes from adding or subtracting delta directions, relevant to whether a single direction can control a feature (V6). It does not measure feature sparsity, overlap, capacity pressure, or whether the model's features are superposed. The stated layer choice and steering coefficients are settings, not separate results.
record.test_reason: The study steers a physics foundation model (Walrus) with difference-of-means directions and judges the outputs qualitatively. It tests the linear representation hypothesis, not superposition. It does not measure sparsity, feature overlap, capacity, polysemanticity, or SAE features. It also never compares 1-D with multi-dimensional features, so V6 (what is superposed are 1-D directions) is not tested. Superposition and polysemanticity appear only in background citations of Toy Models and related work. Under the rules, a steering effect with no measure of the claimed construct is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that difference-of-means single directions in Walrus's latent space correspond to vorticity, diffusion and simulation speed, causally steer predictions, and transfer across systems. They take this as early evidence for domain-general representations and the linear representation hypothesis. They flag the physicality of steered outputs as an open limitation.
record.recipe_differences: The study extracts mean-activation difference directions and injects them to steer a physics foundation model; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method or test capacity competition.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differ between spatially averaged and spatially structured transfer directions. The paper also reports that greater distance from the desired regime requires higher α and can yield distorted, unphysical fields.

fits_no_version.finding: Difference-of-means directions at Walrus's final processor block causally steer vorticity, diffusion and simulation speed. They transfer, when spatially averaged, to Euler, Rayleigh-Bénard and Gray-Scott systems. All outcomes are qualitative visual assessments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear representation hypothesis in scientific (physics) foundation models: concepts are linearly steerable single directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering tensors that keep spatial dimensions give non-linear, sign-mirrored responses: both signs increase convection, and pressure fields invert. Spatially averaged channel-only directions give sign-consistent linear responses (Fig. 5; appendix Figs. 7–8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear steerability depends on whether the steering direction is averaged over spatial positions.

record.peer_reviewed: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025)
record.problems: Results are mainly qualitative visual assessments without reported numerical effect measures or uncertainty estimates. The authors identify physical plausibility of steered results as unresolved; retaining spatial dimensions can produce unrealistic secondary fields. The study focuses on Walrus and the final processor block.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweep or geometry.
All: no capacity or polysemanticity measurement.
All: no neuron-distribution or SAE analysis, and the model is not an LLM.
Whether superposed features are 1-D versus multi-dimensional. Directions are difference-of-means steering vectors, never compared with multi-dimensional alternatives or tied to superposition.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V6 link conflates linear steerability with the superposition-dimensionality claim, so its V6 labels are dropped. Appendix A.1 (Figs. 7–8) gives within-domain results with and without spatial averaging that no row captures. These bear on the linear-representation finding, not on any version listed here. All evidence is qualitative, from single simulation files, with no quantitative measures or uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions; sparsity-dependent transition and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity limits, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or recoverable with a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units.

The study tests causal control using single delta directions, but not whether features are superposed, whether the full feature is one-dimensional rather than multidimensional, or how its results compare with multidimensional feature representations.

rows.subject: Walrus
rows.operation_detail: Subtracted the vortex delta direction during inference.
rows.measure: Qualitative appearance of vorticity in the simulation.
rows.baseline: Unmodified simulation (α=0) displayed two prominent vortical structures.
rows.value: Vortices were progressively suppressed as α increased; the flow became smooth and parallel, characteristic of a laminar regime.
rows.note: Reported as a qualitative visual result; no numerical vorticity measure is given.
rows.check: Steering-control result for the linear representation hypothesis; it does not bear on whether superposed features are 1-D rather than multi-dimensional.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for superposition; progressive vortex suppression is a steering result.
source_check.problem: The measure cannot establish any superposition claim version; versions is none.

rows.subject: Walrus
rows.operation_detail: Added the vortex delta direction during inference.
rows.value: Small injections (approximately 0.1 to 0.4) produced subtle perturbations and incipient rotation; moderate injections (approximately 0.4 to 0.5) yielded well-formed vortices.
rows.note: The authors describe the induction as reliable; the outcome is qualitative.
rows.check: Not a V6 measure. 'numbers_found: 3/3' has no basis in the text. Fig. 3 shows α of 0.2–0.4; the text gives ranges up to 0.5.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for superposition. Section 3.2 gives approximate steering ranges 0.1–0.4 and 0.4–0.5; Figure 3 displays 0, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4.
source_check.problem: Induced vortices establish a steering effect, not any superposition claim version.

rows.subject: Walrus
rows.operation_detail: Added the diffusion delta direction during inference.
rows.measure: Qualitative diffuseness of the fluid interface.
rows.note: The direction was extracted from high- versus low-molecular-diffusion simulations.
rows.check: Not a V6 measure. The frame shown is 30 (Fig. 4 left), which is not recorded.

source_check.problem: Figure 4 does not report an alpha=0 comparison; diffusion steering does not measure superposition.

rows.subject: Walrus
rows.operation_detail: Added the speed delta direction during inference.
rows.value: The vortex formed earlier and was larger and more developed at the displayed frame.
rows.note: The comparison is visual; no measured formation time is reported.

rows.note: The comparison is visual; no measured formation time is reported.

rows.subject: Walrus
rows.operation_detail: Transferred the spatially averaged Shear Flow vortex direction to Rayleigh-Bénard Convection.
rows.measure: Qualitative convection in the buoyancy field.
rows.value: Convection patterns appeared earlier and were larger.
rows.note: The paper also reports a comparatively extreme pressure-field shift.
rows.check: Not a V6 measure (cross-domain transfer of a steering direction).

rows.subject: Walrus
rows.operation_detail: Subtracted the spatially averaged Shear Flow vortex direction from Rayleigh-Bénard Convection.
rows.measure: Qualitative convection in the buoyancy field.
rows.value: Convection decreased relative to the unmodified result.
rows.note: The paper also reports a comparatively extreme pressure-field shift.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for superposition; spatially averaged negative steering decreases convection.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.4, Rayleigh-Bénard Vorticity Transfer; Figure 5 top
source_check.problem: Cross-system steering does not establish any superposition claim version.

rows.subject: Walrus
rows.operation_detail: Transferred the spatially structured Shear Flow vortex direction to Rayleigh-Bénard Convection.
rows.value: Convection increased, but the simple positive-direction/increased-convection relationship did not hold consistently across the two steering signs; large pressure zones appeared.
rows.note: The authors report that both steering signs increased convection in this setting, with high and low pressure zones inverted between results.
rows.check: Not a V6 measure. The 'partial' state reflects that the sign-symmetric steering response failed, not anything about feature dimensionality.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for superposition. With spatial structure retained, both steering signs increase convection and produce inverted pressure zones.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.4, Rayleigh-Bénard Vorticity Transfer; Figure 5 bottom
source_check.problem: Failure of the bidirectional steering relationship does not constitute partial evidence for a superposition claim.

rows.subject: Walrus
rows.operation_detail: Transferred the spatially structured Shear Flow vortex direction to Rayleigh-Bénard Convection.
rows.value: Convection also increased; large high and low pressure zones were inverted relative to the positive-steering result.
rows.note: The negative steering result does not follow a simple decrease-with-negative-direction relationship.
rows.check: Not a V6 measure. Negative steering increased convection, against the expected linear response.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for superposition. Negative steering with spatial structure retained increases convection.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.4, Rayleigh-Bénard Vorticity Transfer; Figure 5 bottom
source_check.problem: The reversal concerns the expected steering response, not any superposition claim version.

relation.reason: Section 1.2 explicitly explains polysemanticity, non-orthogonal feature directions and superposition as background; its own experiments test linear steering.

tranche.reason: The study tests linear representations and causal steering in Walrus, without testing or using superposition, capacity competition, SAE dictionaries or superposed feature dimensionality.

source_check.notes: All outcomes are qualitative steering observations, with no linked superposition version. The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased; physical validity remains an acknowledged limitation.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Within-domain Shear Flow steering and spatially averaged transfers to Euler Quadrant and Gray-Scott
reader_labels.reason: Single extracted delta directions produced the described concept-consistent changes in these settings (r1-r6, r11-r15). This supports directional controllability, not a complete account of superposition or feature dimensionality.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Rayleigh-Bénard transfer with spatial dimensions retained
reader_labels.reason: The negative and positive steering results did not produce the simple opposing changes expected from the direction sign; both increased convection and pressure fields changed strongly (r9-r10).
